Under commit_without_lease=block a branch behind master is refused for files it never touched; under warn it gets false warnings. Fix: run the staged diff in the tree being committed (_this_worktree), not the resolved primary.

data.mechanism: Duplicates share rare domain terms (event kinds, function names, flags); TF-IDF weights them; hard negatives share the same terms, so scores overlap.
data.probe: Benchmarked 13 matchers on 40 dup / 17 related / 18 hard-negative pairs + 98,345 negatives (ddflow log) and speed on run_nemo_run (6,100 records). FTS5 top-50 + rerank: 2.5/5.2 ms. rapidfuzz AP <= 0.29, MinHash 0.27, difflib 0.18, sklearn char TF-IDF 0.46 (203 MB), NLTK Porter 0.531 (no gain).
data.question: Can ddflow detect a duplicate bug/task/lesson at add time without an LLM, and which matcher?

data.alternatives: Warn-only (operator chose ask); reuse task.updated/bug.found for additions (loses simultaneous additions, overwrites bug summaries); close duplicates with a reason only (weakens the regression-test rule); add rapidfuzz/NLTK/scikit-learn (no accuracy gain, allowlist cost).
data.context: Research (2026-10-01, research R-dedupe-matchers): on 40 verified duplicate pairs, 17 related and 18 hard negatives from ddflow's own log, a stdlib TF-IDF cosine (code-aware tokenizer, ~10-line suffix stemmer, ids/shas masked) reranking FTS5 top-50 candidates puts the existing record in the top 3 for 95% (top 5 97.5%), finds the open task that fixes a new bug in the top 3 for 95%, at 2.5 ms median / 5.2 ms p95 per add on run_nemo_run's 6,100 records. NLTK, rapidfuzz, difflib, MinHash and scikit-learn were all no better or worse. A score cannot separate a duplicate from a different bug in the same function (hard negatives 0.43-0.64 sit inside the duplicate band), so ddflow shows candidates and the adding agent or operator answers. Benchmark scripts: the parent session's scratchpad dedup/ (corpus.py, labels.py, matchers.py, bench.py).
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-01: (1) on a match (score >= ask_threshold 0.55 with >= 8 content words, or the text names an existing id) an add is refused until answered new / extends X / duplicate of X / related X: interactive prompt on a TTY, exit 3 with ready commands for scripts, MCP re-call with relation=...; identical text (score 1.0) is recorded as a duplicate of the existing record without asking. Below the threshold candidates >= 0.35 are listed, never asked. (2) Additions and links are NEW event kinds (record.extended, link.recorded) plus link fields on add events; B168 (unknown kinds reported) lands first. extends/duplicate on an open unclaimed record appends to it verbatim with provenance; on a claimed, in-progress or closed record a new linked record is filed and the holder is told in brief. (3) A bug is closed as a duplicate only once X is fixed, citing X's regression test; nothing closes silently. (4) B198 is folded into this phase; B203 is a duplicate of B-semantic-recall. Defaults taken from the research recommendation (operator may revisit): no new runtime dependency (allowlist stays jinja2); every add kind is checked except session prompts and notes; thresholds 0.35 show / 0.55 ask; no LLM confirmation in this phase; the evaluation fixture is a redacted snapshot of real texts; search is within one project's log.
data.title: Every add checks for an existing record and asks; exact copies merge; additions are new event kinds; a duplicate bug closes only once its original is fixed

data.body: From the roborev speed research (2026-10-02; 126 jobs measured): a roborev job takes a median 299 s and p90 963 s, plus queue wait; an agent running 'roborev review --wait' holds its item's lease and file globs throughout (mcp.py was held 40-65 min per task). Design: 'ddflow gate run <id> standards --async' enqueues the job (roborev review <sha> without --wait), records the gate PENDING with the roborev job id, and returns at once; 'ddflow gate collect <id> standards' reads the job's STATUS (never the exit code: 'roborev review --wait -q' exits 1 for findings OR any failure) and records passed / failed(with findings) / unavailable (errored, canceled, timed out, no review stored). Merge and complete refuse while the gate is pending ('pending is not passed'). Leases renew while the item has pending jobs. Acceptance: pending is recorded with the job id and returns in < 5 s; a canceled, errored, timed-out or no-review job collects as unavailable, never passed; merge and complete refuse while pending; a regression test fails against the synchronous gate; CLI and MCP parity test. Reference: roborev wait --job N, roborev show --job N (a review stored after a wrapper timeout is still retrievable).
data.title: Async standards gate: gate run standards --async enqueues the roborev job and records pending; gate collect records the outcome

data.body: From the roborev speed research: agents ran 'timeout 600 roborev review <sha> --wait' and lost reviews (job 943 ran 27 min and stored its review; the 600 s wrapper lost it; 'roborev show --job 943' still had it) and jobs killed by the daemon's 30-minute timeout restart from scratch. Driver text: run 'roborev review <sha>' WITHOUT --wait, then 'roborev wait --job N' with ddflow heartbeats at least every 10 min; read the result with 'roborev show --job N' even after a timeout; never trust the exit code of 'roborev review --wait -q' (1 = findings OR any failure) - read the job status; review only the new tip (range jobs run 2.7x longer than single commits) unless a merge interaction is the point; do not hold file globs longer than the code edit needs. Acceptance: driver and every per-agent delta say so; the help-consistency test passes and every command named exists.

data.body: From the roborev speed research (2026-10-02): since 14ca4ce (B-fix-reviewer-defaults) max_concurrency=0 sends every chunk x hedged copy at once, up to AUTO_CONCURRENCY_CEILING=32, and the shared reviewer endpoint was at 25-40 concurrent requests with per-stream speed falling from 65 to 51 tok/s; roborev is at most 4 of those. Lower the ceiling only if roborev's run time improves by more than ddflow review's slows; record the numbers as research. Never commit endpoint names. data.decision: Operator 2026-10-02 (research R-upstream-reporting): (1) ddflow gains `ddflow bug report` (CLI + MCP `ddflow_bug_report`) and a bug `scope` (project|ddflow); when ddflow or an agent finds/suspects a defect in ddflow itself the operator is PROPOSED an upstream report. (2) Default [upstream].mode = propose (off|propose); NO automatic reporting in v1, not even for mechanical detectors; only the operator can set the mode (an agent's ddflow_configure cannot raise it). (3) The bundle is built by ddflow from allowlisted fields (ddflow version, install kind, commit, python/os, redacted command/exit/traceback with ddflow-relative frames, allowlisted knobs, a minimal aliased log excerpt, provenance) — the agent supplies only a short title and 'what I expected', redacted the same way. NEVER sent: secrets, private IPs/hostnames, home/repo paths, emails, project and repo names, file contents/diffs, operator prompts, item titles/bodies, reviewer endpoints ([upstream].redact_extra adds the operator's own terms). (4) Delivery shipped in v1: a local file (.ddflow/local/reports/), a prefilled GitHub issue URL, AND `gh issue create -R <repo>` when gh is installed and authenticated (unavailable, never silent, otherwise); the REST-with-token and connector routes are later. (5) Who may send: BOTH the CLI (interactive prompt at a terminal) and MCP are possible, MCP being the default surface; consent is always an operator-held credential bound to the digest of the exact rendered text: at a terminal the interactive yes, over MCP a one-time token the operator mints at the terminal (`ddflow bug report approve <id>`) and gives the agent; an agent-supplied 'confirm=true' is NEVER consent; any edit after the yes invalidates it; per submission, never per session. (6) Fix proposals: when the agent has ddflow's source (own dev tree or a configured [upstream].source), the fix is made on a branch with a failing-first regression test through ddflow's normal gates and delivered as a `git format-patch` file in .ddflow/local/reports/; ddflow NEVER pushes or opens a PR; a fork PR would need its own explicit per-submission yes in a later decision. (7) The dev tree itself: bugs stay in the local queue; the upstream mirror is optional. (8) Records `bug.reported_upstream` (url, number, delivery, time, digest) close the loop later.

chunk_findings.detail: Private IPv4 addresses written with leading zeros are not redacted. `_is_private` calls `ipaddress.IPv4Address(raw)`, but Python’s `ipaddress` module rejects zero-padded octets with `ValueError`. The `except ValueError` returns `False`, so the `keep` predicate returns `True` and the match is left unchanged. For example, `redact_report("connect to 172.16.001.1")` returns the string with `172.16.001.1` still present; the acceptance criterion that no 172.16–31.x address remains is violated. The same happens for `010.0.0.1`, `192.168.001.1`, etc. The `private_addresses` helper inherits the same blind spot.

chunk_findings.detail: The change description states the redaction must remove "private IPv4/IPv6 and `.lan`/`.local`/`.internal`/`home.arpa` hosts", and the test module's own fixture relies on `.local` being redacted (`printer." + "local`, enforced only by `out.counts["host"] == 4`). However `_leaks`, the leak detector used by the main acceptance test `test_every_bug_summary_and_rendering_is_clean`, matches only `lan|internal|home\.arpa` and omits `local`. Since the synthetic test's `.local` coverage comes from a hardcoded `counts["host"] == 4`, the corpus loop over real `bug.found` summaries has no `.local` detector at all. Concrete failure: a real event whose `data.summary` contains e.g. `nas.local` will, if `redact_report` regresses and leaves it visible, still produce `_leaks(out.text) == []` (the hostname check uses only `host`, the `.lan` regex ignores `.local`, and `_corpus_projects` only matches `src|git|code|work|projects` path segments), so `assert not left` passes and the `.local` host leaks out undetected by the very test that is supposed to guarantee "no ... .local ... leaves in a report". The other three suffixes from the stated detector list are present in the same alternation, which indicates `local` was dropped from the list rather than deliberately excluded.

data.body: Operator question 2026-10-02: can the version live in one place instead of ddflow/__init__.py, ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py (SERVER_INFO), pyproject.toml and server.json (version, the pypi package version, two OCI identifier tags) -- plus uv.lock, which records the project's own version and is re-locked on every bump. Investigated (see the scratch probe): with hatchling,  and  the wheel/sdist take the version from __init__.py (verified: a scratch project built demo_mcp-0.1.10 after editing only __init__.py), AND uv.lock then carries NO version for the project, so a bump no longer touches uv.lock (verified:  passes after the version changes). Runtime reads it by plain import (no importlib.metadata: stale in editable/PYTHONPATH source runs, which ddflow's hook script and worktrees use). Design: (1) single literal  in ddflow/__init__.py; (2) pyproject.toml dynamic version; (3) mcp.py SERVER_INFO built from __version__; (4) server.json becomes a generated, committed artifact: a template server.template.json with a version placeholder (also in the OCI identifier tags and the pypi package version; OCI packages carry NO version field, see B-fix-registry-oci-version) rendered by scripts/render_server_json.py (stdlib; a --check mode); CI renders it in / before publish and a test fails if the committed file differs from the render; (5) scripts/bump.sh edits only __init__.py then renders server.json (no uv re-lock); (6) every place that greps pyproject.toml for  (publish.yml gate/pypi jobs, release.sh, bump.sh, tests/test_packaging.py::test_the_declared_versions_agree) reads __init__.py instead; (7) the primary .venv editable metadata is stale until a reinstall -- code must not depend on it. data.body:
Operator question 2026-10-02: can the version live in one place instead of ddflow/__init__.py, ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py (SERVER_INFO), pyproject.toml and server.json (version, the pypi package version, two OCI identifier tags) -- plus uv.lock, which records the project's own version and is re-locked on every bump.

Investigated with a scratch project (read-only probe): with hatchling, `dynamic = ["version"]` and `[tool.hatch.version] path = "ddflow/__init__.py"`, the wheel and sdist take the version from __init__.py (a scratch project built demo_mcp-0.1.10 after editing only __init__.py), AND uv.lock then carries NO version for the project, so a bump no longer touches uv.lock (`uv lock --check` passes after the version changes). Runtime reads it by plain import (no importlib.metadata: stale in editable / PYTHONPATH source runs, which ddflow's hook script and worktrees use).

Design: (1) a single literal __version__ in ddflow/__init__.py; (2) pyproject.toml dynamic version; (3) mcp.py SERVER_INFO built from __version__; (4) server.json becomes a generated, committed artifact: a template server.template.json with a version placeholder (also in the OCI identifier tags and the pypi package version; OCI packages carry NO version field, see B-fix-registry-oci-version) rendered by scripts/render_server_json.py (stdlib; a --check mode); CI renders it in the gate/verify jobs before publish and a test fails if the committed file differs from the render; (5) scripts/bump.sh edits only __init__.py then renders server.json (no uv re-lock); (6) every place that greps pyproject.toml for the version line (publish.yml gate and pypi jobs, release.sh, bump.sh, tests/test_packaging.py::test_the_declared_versions_agree) reads __init__.py instead; (7) the primary .venv editable metadata is stale until a reinstall -- code must not depend on it.

Rejected: hatch-vcs / git-tag versions (CI bumps by commit and creates the tag AFTER publishing); importlib.metadata at runtime (stale in source trees); making pyproject the single source (it is not shipped in the wheel, so a runtime read needs two code paths).

Acceptance (failing-first): after editing ONLY ddflow/__init__.py and running render_server_json.py, `uv build` yields that version, `ddflow --version` and the MCP serverInfo agree, server.json carries it in version, the pypi package and both OCI tags, `uv lock --check` passes, and tests/test_packaging.py holds; a test fails when server.json is not the render of the template; the publish workflow's version steps read __init__.py (actionlint clean); README "Cutting a release" section updated (D-readme-current).

Core requirements: the template renderer is a jinja2.sandbox.SandboxedEnvironment (StrictUndefined, trim_blocks, lstrip_blocks, no autoescape) fed ONLY plain data from the kind's pure query function plus a small documented filter set (md_escape, wrap, date, truncate, bar); no repo handle, no objects with methods; the resolution order [export.<doc>].template -> .ddflow/templates/export/<kind>.md.j2 -> shipped (reuse services/prompts.py resolution, do not duplicate); a template error is a 'could not run' (exit 2) outcome and nothing is written; the data contract per kind has a `schema_version` exposed to the template; the header (marker + body digest) is added by ddflow AROUND the template output so a template cannot remove hand-edit protection; record a digest of the shipped template an override was ejected from.
